scope: Supplement D.2.a, Eqs. (D1)–(D3). Each local Bell projector is an amplitude outer product. For every positive trace-one n-qubit density matrix the Born weights of the full product Bell measurement on two copies are nonnegative and sum to one.
Supplement D.2.b, Eqs. (D5)–(D6). The shared Bell measurement record gives a sign in {−1,1} with expectation |Tr(Pρ)|² for every subsequently specified Pauli P.
Supplement D.2.b, Lemma 1, Eq. (D8). For N>0 independent two-copy Bell rounds on any density operator and each u>0, the chance of a squared-expectation error at least u is at most 2 exp(−Nu²/2).
Supplement D.2.b, Eqs. (D9)–(D10). The squared error of the clipped square-root estimator for y≥0 is bounded by the absolute error in estimating y².

Supplement D.2.b, Corollary 1, Eq. (D11), the quantum upper half of Theorem 6. For every n-qubit state and each Pauli revealed after collection, 2,048 Bell rounds on 4,096 copies give additive magnitude error at most 1/4 with success probability at least 4/5.

Supplement D.4, Task 1. Distinct Pauli words are Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal. For the normalized state (I+aP)/2ⁿ, |a|≤1, the nonidentity query Q has expectation of magnitude |a| if Q=P and zero otherwise.

Supplement D.4, Task 1, Eq. (D39), quantum upper bound at failure probability 1/5. For every hidden sign and distinct nonidentity pair P,Q, 256 Bell rounds (512 copies) select the larger magnitude in both label orderings using the same record. Theorem 7 concerns the conventional lower bound.
